Sheboygan County, Wisconsin tax deed sale happens when the county takes ownership of a property because the owner did not pay real estate taxes. The county then sells that property to the public, usually through a sealed bid process. This guide walks through how it works, what to check before you bid, and where to find current information.

What Is a Tax Deed?

When a property owner does not pay real estate taxes, the debt becomes delinquent. If the taxes stay unpaid long enough, the county can take legal title to the property. This is called a tax deed. The county then sells these properties to the public to recover the unpaid taxes.

What Is a Tax Deed in Sheboygan County?

When someone stops paying property taxes in Sheboygan County, the debt does not just disappear. It grows year after year. If the owner never catches up, the county has the legal right to take the property. This is called tax foreclosure, and the result is a tax deed.

Wisconsin does not sell tax lien certificates the way some other states do. There is no third party who buys the debt and waits to collect interest. Instead, Sheboygan County takes full legal title to the property first. Only after that does the county turn around and sell it to a new buyer. So the term “tax deed” means the county already owns the property outright by the time it lists it for sale.

Key Takeaways

  • Sheboygan County tax deed sales occur when property taxes go unpaid, leading to county ownership before public sale.
  • The Sheboygan County Treasurer’s Office manages the tax deed sale process through sealed bids, not live auctions.
  • Potential bidders should research properties thoroughly and understand they are sold ‘as is,’ with no guarantees from the county.
  • Next tax deed sales are not expected until spring 2027, as there are currently no foreclosed properties available.
  • To bid, follow official announcements, download necessary forms, and submit bids before strict deadlines.

Who Handles the Sheboygan County Tax Deed Sale?

The Sheboygan County Treasurer’s Office runs this process. This office also handles regular property tax collection, tax bill lookups, and lottery credit questions. When a foreclosure is complete and the county holds a group of properties, the Treasurer’s Office opens a sale window and invites sealed bids from the public.

How the Process Moves Forward

Sheboygan County does not run a rolling, year-round auction. Instead, it groups foreclosed properties and opens a sale window only when it has a batch ready. As of now, the county’s Treasurer’s Office is not currently holding any tax foreclosed property in its inventory, so the next sale is not expected until after the next foreclosure action wraps up, likely in spring 2027. This means timing matters a lot if you want to bid on a Sheboygan County tax deed property.

How to Bid on a Sheboygan County Tax Deed Property

Follow these steps when a sale window opens.

  1. Watch the county’s Treasurer page.

    Sheboygan County posts sale announcements and bid forms on its Tax Foreclosed Property for Sale page.

  2. Download the bid form and property list.

    Each active sale posts links with property details and the exact bid form you need to fill out.

  3. Research the parcel first.

    Use the Land Records and Tax Web Portal to check ownership history, past tax bills, and assessment data before you commit to a bid.

  4. Check zoning and condition.

    Contact the local town, village, or city where the parcel sits to confirm what the land can be used for.

  5. Submit a sealed bid before the deadline.

    Sales run on strict cutoff times, often 4:00 pm on the closing date. Late bids are not accepted.

  6. Wait for the county’s decision.

    The Treasurer’s Office reviews all sealed bids and awards the property to the winning bidder.

  7. Close and record the deed.

    Once payment is confirmed, the county transfers the deed, which you then record with the Register of Deeds.

Why Buyers Should Slow Down and Check Everything

Tax deed properties sell “as is.” Sheboygan County makes no promises about the roof, the foundation, old debts tied to the land, or anything else. Before you send in a bid, take these steps:

  • Look up the parcel on the county’s online Land Records portal for ownership and tax history.
  • Search Register of Deeds records for old liens, judgments, or claims that never got cleared.
  • Drive by the property. Interior access is rarely offered before a sale closes.
  • Call the local zoning office to confirm the property can legally be used the way you plan to use it.
  • Set aside extra money for repairs, cleanup, or unpaid utility charges tied to the property.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Sheboygan County, Wisconsin tax deed?

It is the ownership title the county receives after a property owner fails to pay real estate taxes long enough to trigger foreclosure. The county then resells the property to the public.

Does Sheboygan County sell tax lien certificates?

No. Like other Wisconsin counties, Sheboygan County does not sell liens. It takes full title to the property, then sells the property itself.

How does Sheboygan County sell tax foreclosed property?

Through a sealed bid process managed by the Treasurer’s Office. Bids are due by a stated deadline, and the county reviews them afterward rather than running a live auction.

Is there a tax deed sale happening right now?

Not at this time. The county has no foreclosed properties in inventory and does not expect another sale until after the next foreclosure action finishes, likely in spring 2027. Check the county’s page for updates.

Can I inspect a property before bidding?

Usually only from the outside. Properties sell “as is,” and interior walkthroughs are typically not offered.
